title: Imperfect subjunctive and hypotheticals
objectives: I can form the imperfect subjunctive of regular and irregular verbs from the third person plural of the preterite.
I can talk about unreal or unlikely situations with se + imperfect subjunctive + conditional.
I can give advice with Se eu fosse você and express past wishes and requests with queria que and pediu que.
I can express wishes with Quem me dera, Quem dera and Tomara que, and use como se.

dialogues.title: E se a gente ganhasse na loteria?
dialogues.context: Three friends have lunch together and play the game of what they would do with a lottery prize.

lines.speaker: Natália
lines.pt: Gente, se vocês ganhassem na loteria, o que fariam?
lines.en: Guys, if you won the lottery, what would you do?

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Eu largaria o emprego no mesmo dia e viajaria pelo mundo.
lines.en: I would quit my job the same day and travel around the world.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Eu não largaria. Se eu tivesse todo esse dinheiro, abriria um negócio.
lines.en: I wouldn't quit. If I had all that money, I would start a business.

lines.speaker: Natália
lines.pt: Que tipo de negócio?
lines.en: What kind of business?

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Uma padaria. Quem me dera ter coragem de abrir uma agora!
lines.en: A bakery. If only I had the courage to open one now!

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Se eu fosse você, começaria pequeno, só com um carrinho de café.
lines.en: If I were you, I would start small, just with a coffee cart.

lines.speaker: Natália
lines.pt: Eu compraria uma casinha na praia e viveria com calma.
lines.en: I would buy a little house on the beach and live peacefully.

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Quem dera a gente pudesse fazer isso de verdade.
lines.en: If only we could really do that.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Se a gente economizasse um pouco mais, talvez desse.
lines.en: If we saved a little more, maybe it could work.

lines.speaker: Natália
lines.pt: Então vamos começar a guardar dinheiro hoje!
lines.en: Then let's start saving money today!

dialogues.title: Uma proposta em Lisboa
dialogues.context: Priscila has been offered a job in Lisbon and asks her friend Eduardo for advice.

lines.speaker: Priscila
lines.pt: Eduardo, recebi uma proposta de emprego em Lisboa. Não sei o que fazer.
lines.en: Eduardo, I received a job offer in Lisbon. I don't know what to do.

lines.speaker: Eduardo
lines.pt: Se eu fosse você, aceitaria. É uma grande oportunidade.
lines.en: If I were you, I would accept. It's a great opportunity.

lines.speaker: Priscila
lines.pt: Mas eu queria que minha família pudesse ir comigo.
lines.en: But I wish my family could go with me.

lines.speaker: Eduardo
lines.pt: Entendo. Se eles pudessem, iriam sem pensar. Mas vocês podem se visitar com frequência.
lines.en: I understand. If they could, they would go without thinking. But you can visit each other often.

lines.speaker: Priscila
lines.pt: Meu pai pediu que eu pensasse bem antes de decidir.
lines.en: My father asked me to think carefully before deciding.

lines.speaker: Eduardo
lines.pt: Ele tem razão. Se eu estivesse no seu lugar, faria uma lista de prós e contras.
lines.en: He's right. If I were in your place, I would make a list of pros and cons.

lines.speaker: Priscila
lines.pt: Boa ideia. E o salário? Se fosse menor, eu não aceitaria.
lines.en: Good idea. And the salary? If it were lower, I wouldn't accept.

lines.speaker: Eduardo
lines.pt: Mas é maior! Se você ficasse aqui, demoraria anos para ganhar isso.
lines.en: But it's higher! If you stayed here, it would take years to earn that.

lines.speaker: Priscila
lines.pt: Tá bom, vou decidir até sexta. Obrigada pelo conselho.
lines.en: Okay, I'll decide by Friday. Thanks for the advice.

dialogues.title: Arrependimentos e sonhos
dialogues.context: Sérgio and Renata, both in their forties, talk about the lives they might have lived.

lines.speaker: Renata
lines.pt: Sérgio, você já pensou em como seria sua vida se fosse músico?
lines.en: Sérgio, have you ever thought about what your life would be like if you were a musician?

lines.speaker: Sérgio
lines.pt: Penso sempre. Se eu fosse músico, estaria tocando em algum bar agora, e não numa sala de escritório.
lines.en: All the time. If I were a musician, I would be playing in some bar now, and not in an office room.

lines.speaker: Renata
lines.pt: Você ainda toca violão?
lines.en: Do you still play the guitar?

lines.speaker: Sérgio
lines.pt: Pouco. Se eu tivesse mais tempo livre, tocaria todo dia.
lines.en: Little. If I had more free time, I would play every day.

lines.speaker: Renata
lines.pt: Eu também tenho meus arrependimentos. Eu queria que meus pais me deixassem morar no exterior quando eu era jovem.
lines.en: I have my regrets too. I wanted my parents to let me live abroad when I was young.

lines.speaker: Sérgio
lines.pt: Ah, quem dera a gente pudesse voltar no tempo!
lines.en: Ah, if only we could go back in time!

lines.speaker: Renata
lines.pt: Seria bom, né? Mas as pessoas falam como se fosse simples mudar de vida depois dos quarenta.
lines.en: That would be nice, right? But people talk as if it were simple to change your life after forty.

lines.speaker: Sérgio
lines.pt: Não é impossível. Se você quisesse, ainda poderia viajar por um ano.
lines.en: It's not impossible. If you wanted to, you could still travel for a year.

lines.speaker: Renata
lines.pt: Quem sabe. Vou pensar nisso com calma.
lines.en: Who knows. I'll think about it calmly.

lines.speaker: Sérgio
lines.pt: Pense mesmo. Ninguém deveria viver com arrependimento.
lines.en: Do think about it. Nobody should live with regret.

grammar.title: Forming the imperfect subjunctive
grammar.explanation:
The imperfect subjunctive is built exactly like the future subjunctive: take the eles form of the preterite, remove -ram and add -sse. So falaram gives falasse, comeram gives comesse, partiram gives partisse. The endings are -sse for eu, você, ele and ela, -ssemos for nós, and -ssem for vocês and eles. In regions that use tu, add -sses (falasses).

The nós form always carries a written accent on the vowel before -ssemos: falássemos, comêssemos, partíssemos, tivéssemos, fôssemos. This is a very common spelling error, so learn it with the form.

Irregular verbs use the irregular preterite stem, which is why the same stems keep reappearing: tiveram, tivesse; fizeram, fizesse; disseram, dissesse; puderam, pudesse; vieram, viesse. Ser and ir share fosse, and ver gives visse while vir gives viesse. The imperfect subjunctive is used for unreal, unlikely or past-viewpoint situations; it never refers to a real, completed past event.

examples.en: If I spoke French, I would work in Paris.

examples.pt: Se vocês comessem menos, dormiriam melhor.
examples.en: If you ate less, you would sleep better.

examples.en: If we had a car, we would go to the beach.

examples.en: If he were more patient, he would be a good teacher.

examples.pt: Se ela viesse, a festa seria perfeita.
examples.en: If she came, the party would be perfect.

grammar.title: Hypothetical conditions: se + imperfect subjunctive + conditional
grammar.explanation:
To talk about something unreal, unlikely or contrary to the present, put the se clause in the imperfect subjunctive and the result in the conditional (futuro do pretérito): Se eu tivesse tempo, viajaria mais. The conditional is formed by adding -ia, -ia, -íamos, -iam to the infinitive: viajaria, comeria, partiria. Fazer, dizer and trazer lose the -ze- syllable: faria, diria, traria.

Compare this with an open possibility, which uses the future subjunctive: Se eu tiver tempo, vou viajar (maybe I will). The imperfect subjunctive signals that the speaker does not expect it to happen, or that it is pure imagination.

In everyday speech, many Brazilians replace the conditional in the result clause by the imperfect indicative or ir + infinitive: Se eu tivesse tempo, viajava; Se eu tivesse tempo, eu ia viajar. Both are very natural in conversation. The imperfect subjunctive in the se clause is not replaceable. Se eu fosse você is the standard formula for giving advice: Se eu fosse você, não aceitaria.

rows: se + future subjunctive, present or future
Se eu tiver tempo, vou viajar.

grammar.title: Past requests and wishes: queria que, pediu que, esperava que
grammar.explanation:
When the main verb of a sentence is in a past tense or in the conditional, the verb in the que clause also moves back in time: it takes the imperfect subjunctive instead of the present subjunctive. Compare Quero que você venha (present) with Queria que você viesse (past or polite). This is the sequence of tenses rule.

The pattern works with all the triggers you know: Ela pediu que eu esperasse (She asked me to wait), Eu esperava que ele gostasse (I was hoping he would like it), Era importante que a gente soubesse (It was important that we knew), Duvidava que ela chegasse (I doubted she would arrive).

Eu queria que... is also a gentle way to make a request in the present. It sounds softer than Quero que...: Eu queria que você me ajudasse (I'd like you to help me). In conversation, pedir with an infinitive is common too: Ela pediu pra eu esperar. Como se (as if) always takes the imperfect subjunctive: Ele age como se fosse o dono.

examples.en: I wish you would call me more.

examples.en: She asked me to wait at the door.

examples.en: My parents hoped that I would study medicine.

examples.en: It was important that everyone knew the truth.

examples.pt: Ele fala como se fosse especialista.
examples.en: He talks as if he were an expert.

grammar.title: Wish expressions: quem me dera, quem dera, tomara que
grammar.explanation:
Brazilians express wishes about the unreal or the unlikely with a few short formulas. Quem me dera and quem dera mean 'if only' or 'I wish'. They are followed by an infinitive (Quem me dera ter mais tempo) or by a subject plus the imperfect subjunctive (Quem dera eu pudesse viajar mais).

Tomara que has a range. Followed by the present subjunctive it expresses a hope about something possible: Tomara que ele venha amanhã. Followed by the imperfect subjunctive it suggests that the hope is remote or probably false: Tomara que fosse verdade (I wish it were true).

A wish can also stand alone with se: Ah, se eu pudesse! (If only I could!). This sentence deliberately leaves the result clause unspoken. Use these forms with the imperfect subjunctive when the situation is contrary to reality now: Quem dera estivéssemos de férias (If only we were on vacation) refers to a present fact that is the opposite of the wish.

Quem dera eu pudesse viajar mais.

culture.title: Se eu fosse você, Mega-Sena and the Brazilian dream
culture.text:
The phrase Se eu fosse você is so familiar in Brazil that it became the title of a hit comedy film in 2006, in which a husband and wife swap bodies and see life from each other's point of view. The expression is the standard way to give friendly advice, and its softness is typical of Brazilian conversation: instead of saying 'You should accept', people say Se eu fosse você, aceitaria.

Dreams about money are a national pastime. The Mega-Sena lottery draws huge crowds to lottery shops (casas lotéricas) when the prize reaches a very high amount, and people ask each other Se você ganhasse, o que faria? Two classic dreams are the casa própria (owning your own home) and the décimo terceiro salário, an extra month of pay that most formal employees receive in December and spend on gifts, debts or travel.

Brazilians also use Quem me dera and Tomara que in songs and ordinary speech to talk about distant wishes. In conversation, the conditional is often replaced by the imperfect (Se eu tivesse dinheiro, eu viajava), a pattern that is natural in speech but less common in formal writing.

readings.title: E se eu morasse no exterior?

paragraphs.pt: Quando eu era jovem, queria que o tempo passasse mais devagar. Hoje, aos quarenta anos, às vezes imagino como seria minha vida se eu morasse no exterior.
paragraphs.en: When I was young, I wanted time to pass more slowly. Today, at forty, I sometimes imagine what my life would be like if I lived abroad.

paragraphs.pt: Se eu morasse em outro país, falaria outra língua todos os dias e conheceria pessoas de lugares muito diferentes. Talvez eu me sentisse sozinha, mas aprenderia muito.
paragraphs.en: If I lived in another country, I would speak another language every day and meet people from very different places. Maybe I would feel lonely, but I would learn a lot.

paragraphs.pt: Meu marido diz que eu falo como se fosse fácil. Ele tem razão: se tivéssemos filhos pequenos, não poderíamos mudar assim. Mas nossos filhos já são adultos, e isso muda tudo.
paragraphs.en: My husband says I talk as if it were easy. He's right: if we had small children, we couldn't move like that. But our children are already adults, and that changes everything.

paragraphs.pt: Uma amiga me deu um conselho: se eu fosse você, começaria com uma viagem longa. Se você gostasse, poderia pensar em algo maior.
paragraphs.en: A friend gave me a piece of advice: if I were you, I would start with a long trip. If you liked it, you could think about something bigger.

paragraphs.pt: Quem me dera ter coragem agora mesmo! Por enquanto, estou economizando um pouco todo mês. Quem sabe, daqui a dois anos, meu sonho deixe de ser só um sonho.
paragraphs.en: If only I had the courage right now! For the time being, I'm saving a little every month. Who knows, two years from now my dream will stop being just a dream.
